To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human fixed-interval schedules of reinforcement can be modified by the imposition of constraints on the number of responses and/or session duration.

human fixed-interval behavior is affected by instructions to constrain the number of responses per reinforcement and by the duration of the session, and that the effects of instructions are mediated by the effects of these constraints on the rate of responding.

the effects of instructional constraints on fixed-interval performance are dependent on the type and number of constraints imposed, and the effects of instructions to minimize the duration of the session are more powerful in reducing post-reinforcement pauses than instructions to minimize the number of responses per session.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of instructions on the behavior of human subjects exposed to a fixed-interval reinforcement schedule.
the effects of instructional constraints on the performance of a fixed-interval (FI) schedule of reinforcement.
a variety of issues related to the effects of instructional constraints on the performance of humans in a fixed-interval schedule of reinforcement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

human subjects are capable of responding in ways which are sensitive to the contingencies of reinforcement, even though their behavior is constrained by the demands and contingencies of the experimental situation.
the effects of instructions on human fixed-intervals are complex and variable.
human fixed-interval behavior is not fixed-interval behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human organism is capable of a diversity of patterns of FI performance.
the effects of the instructions to minimize session length and to minimize response rate are additive.
the human subject is a very complex organism and the effects of instructions on human behavior can be quite varied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the imposition of constraints on the number of responses and/or the duration on the fixed interval schedule of reinforcement can alter the pattern of performance.
the human fixed-interval schedule of reinforcement is a powerful experimental tool for studying behavior.
human subjects exposed to a fixed-interval schedule are highly sensitive to the presence and absence of instructions, and to the nature of the instructional contingencies.
